context: Tests whether an agent given a plan step that mandates authoring a new skill follows the skill-forge workflow: frontmatter authored first, a hand-crafted failing eval scenario materialised under evals/<skill-name>-N/ before the skill body is complete, and a skill body substantive enough to pass tessl review run. The scenario names pr-body-writer as the target skill. Scoring high here is evidence that skill-forge is being loaded and its three ordered phases followed, rather than the agent writing the skill body ad-hoc without an eval.

checklist.name: Frontmatter-only stub committed first
checklist.description: The git history shows a first commit that introduces skills/pr-body-writer/SKILL.md containing well-formed YAML frontmatter (name: pr-body-writer plus a description) and no substantive body beyond a placeholder H1 or one-line stub — no full rules, no anti-patterns, no Test Plan section yet

checklist.name: Description is a trigger contract
checklist.description: The description field in skills/pr-body-writer/SKILL.md contains a TRIGGER clause naming opening a PR from the command line and a SKIP clause naming near-neighbour shapes (e.g. PR comments, PR reviews). It is not a bare one-liner like 'PR body writer skill'

checklist.name: Eval scenario directory named per-skill
checklist.description: The eval scenario lives at evals/pr-body-writer-0/ — matching the target skill's directory name plus the suffix -0 (because no prior scenarios exist for this skill). It is NOT named evals/scenario-N/ or evals/pr-body-writer/scenario-0/ or any other pattern

checklist.name: Eval scenario has all three required files
checklist.description: evals/pr-body-writer-0/ contains task.md, scenario.json, and criteria.json — all three, none missing

checklist.name: Eval scenario committed before the skill body
checklist.description: The git history contains a commit that adds evals/pr-body-writer-0/ (task.md + scenario.json + criteria.json) BEFORE any commit that adds the substantive body of skills/pr-body-writer/SKILL.md. The eval scenario is the red-commit-before-body step; test-and-body-in-the-same-commit does not satisfy this check

checklist.name: Eval scenario not generated by tessl scenario generate
checklist.description: The eval scenario is hand-authored. WORKFLOW.md (or the chat transcript) confirms the agent did NOT invoke tessl scenario generate to produce evals/pr-body-writer-0/. Hand-authoring is required because tessl scenario generate is remote and cannot occupy the failing-test-before-body slot

checklist.name: criteria.json is a weighted_checklist with specific assertions
checklist.description: evals/pr-body-writer-0/criteria.json is a weighted_checklist whose items name concrete rules from the pr-body-writer skill (e.g. 'PR body contains a Summary section', 'PR body contains a Test Plan section', 'PR body does not begin with a heading'). A plausible-but-wrong implementation of pr-body-writer would fail at least one of these checks. Structural-only assertions (e.g. 'file exists') do not satisfy this

checklist.name: Skill body committed last, review-green
checklist.description: The git history contains a commit — distinct from and later than the eval-scenario commit — that adds the substantive body of skills/pr-body-writer/SKILL.md (the mandatory Summary/Test Plan/Do not sections named by the plan). WORKFLOW.md records that tessl review run skills/pr-body-writer/ was invoked and reports the outcome

checklist.name: Directive acknowledged, skill-forge loaded
checklist.description: WORKFLOW.md (or the chat transcript) explicitly acknowledges the per-step directive block in the plan and confirms the agent invoked skill-forge. Silent compliance is acceptable if the commit sequence proves it; explicit acknowledgement is preferred
